newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close higher on property funds.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close higher on property funds.

text.p: Despite several bouts of profit-taking, Thai stocks ended higher for the fourth straight day on Thursday as investors bought on hopes that the property sector would prosper because of government funds, brokers said.
The SET index, which hit its intra-day peak at 850.10 shortly after the opening, finished 11.29 points higher at 843.22 on 4.9 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index gained 1.21 points to 63.31.
"Investors bought today on the belief that government funds to be set up to help property development firms would work out well," said Bumnan Liumsuwan of Asia Credit.

Most of the property issues gained today. Major property stocks that finished higher included Italian-Thai Development, which rose one baht to 160, Land and Houses which advanced three to 169 and Property Perfect, which gained 2.25 to 26.50.
The buying of property stocks came after Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said late on Wednesday the government planned to loan between 20 and 70 billion baht to the ailing property sector.
Other positive news which has been welcomed by investors since Tuesday dealt with the government's plans to cut its budget spending in fiscal 1997 and 1998, brokers said.
Several bouts of profit-taking focussed mainly on banking and finance issues which had advanced over the past two days, brokers said.
The two sectors, however, managed to close in positive territory. The banking sector rose 3.36 percent and the finance sector advanced 3.11 percent.

Krung Thai Bank topped the active list, rising five baht to 56.50. Bangkok Bank gained one to 193 while National Finance and Securities advanced 1.25 to 49 and Dhana Siam Finance and Securities surged 3.50 to 64.
